subject: use of stat_summary with a factor

messages.author: c91a208fffacfb7e
messages.subject: use of stat_summary with a factor
parts:
I often use plots like the enclosed to describe the between- and
within-group variability in data. (The line joins the average
responses for each group). That plot was created with lattice as

data(Dyestuff, package="lme4")
dotplot(reorder(Batch, Yield) ~ Yield, Dyestuff,
ylab = "Batch", jitter.y = TRUE, pch = 21, aspect = 0.32,
xlab = "Yield of dyestuff (grams of standard color)",
type = c("p", "a"))

I tried to create a similar plot using ggplot2 and got as far as

qplot(reorder(Batch, Yield), Yield, data=Dyestuff,
geom="point", pch=21, xlab=NULL,
ylab="Yield of dyestuff (grams of standard color)") +
stat_summary(fun.y = mean, geom="line") + coord_flip()

but the line I was hoping for didn't materialize. Earlier I had used
position=position_jitter(w=0.1,h=0) in the call to qplot() but I
pulled it in case the jittered values were considered the x values
when grouping the y's. However, even without the jittering I seem to
be unable to add the line, perhaps because one scale is a factor.

Suggestions welcome.

messages.author: 45a85351148578ad
messages.subject: RE: use of stat_summary with a factor
parts:
Dear Prof Bates,

I think you are correct about the need for a continuous x scale:

qplot(x = reorder(Batch, Yield), y = Yield, data=Dyestuff,

geom="point", pch=21, xlab=NULL,
ylab="Yield of dyestuff (grams of standard color)") +
stat_summary( aes( x = as.numeric( reorder(Batch, Yield) ) ), fun.y =

mean, geom="line") +
coord_flip()

Hope this helps,
fernando

messages.subject: Re: use of stat_summary with a factor

Use group=1:
stat_summary(fun.y = mean, geom="line", aes(group=1))

Best,
Ista
